newsitem.title: UK: Oftel plans new condition for BT licence.
newsitem.headline: Oftel plans new condition for BT licence.

text.p: Oftel plans a new licence condition to prevent British Telecommunications Plc from jeopardising its ability to provide and finance domestic services as it expands internationally, the UK telecoms watchdog said on Thursday.
Under the proposals, BT's directors will have to submit a certificate each year stating whether they have done anything that may cause a breach of the condition.

The Director General of Oftel will also be able to require an auditor's report from BT stating whether it has in place and is following the systems and processes necessary for the certificate to be produced.
"I welcome the fact that BT is becoming a global company," said Oftel Director General Don Cruickshank.
"However, I have a duty to make sure that, as BT expands its interests overseas, it can continue to fulfil its obligations to customers and other telecoms operators in the UK," he added.
BT is in the process of completing a $20 billion merger with America's MCI Communications Corp.

Cruickshank said in March the risk of BT's overseas activities adversely affecting its ability to meet its UK obligations was small but could not be ignored. He said developments since then had underlined the need for extra regulatory vigilance.
The BT-MCI deal has run into complications after MCI said it was expecting losses from its expansion into local telecoms to total $800 million this year -- double previous estimates.
A statutory consultation period on the Oftel proposals now follows.
